interface.title: BioCompiler V0 — Executable cell-fate dynamics: compile a temporary control into a persistent phenotype transition
interface.field: Systems biology / gene regulatory network dynamics (haematopoietic cell-fate control, GATA1–PU.1–GATA2 circuit)
interface.stage_of_work: In-silico hypothesis generation and model reproduction, before any wet-lab design
interface.what_it_is_for: It searches a fixed library of temporary interventions on a published 3-gene ODE model and finds the ones that move the system from one stable phenotype to another and keep it there after the control is released, then ranks the alternatives.

data.note: Everything is generated from the built-in published model (wu_zhou_tian_2022_equation_6, Wu, Zhou & Tian 2022, eq. 6 with supplementary tables 3–7). There are no uploads or sign-ins. Each compile took several minutes of CPU simulation on this server.

tree.general: Find temporary interventions that permanently switch a dynamical system from one stable state to another, and compare the alternatives by cost and closeness to the target
tree.specific: Compile temporary controls that move the GATA1/PU.1/GATA2 model between phenotype attractors (G1H, P1H, G2H, LE3G) and persist after washout. Robustness scores appear only in the Reachability atlas, which did not finish in this session, so trustworthiness was not judged here.

features.name: Start/target state request with constraint panel
features.general: Pick a start state and a different target state, cap how many variables may be manipulated, exclude some variables, choose a ranking objective, then launch an exhaustive search. Changing any setting clears the stale result.
features.specific: In the sidebar, set Starting phenotype and Desired phenotype (the start is removed from the target list), Maximum controlled regulators (1/2), Do not control (multiselect of GATA1/PU1/GATA2 with Select all) and Ranking objective (Robustness First / Sparsity First), then press Compile transition. The 'Move X to Y, then release the control' sentence updates live.
steps: choose Starting phenotype
choose Desired phenotype (the start is excluded)
set max controlled regulators and forbidden regulators
choose Robustness First or Sparsity First
press Compile transition; any later change clears the result
serves_tasks: Choose the start and target states and run the full search with default constraints
Repeat the design for a second target under a forbidden variable and a cost-first ranking

features.name: Compiled-transition summary with ranked alternatives table
features.general: After a search, show headline metrics for the best solution (number of successes, variables used, cost), its label and closeness to target, and a sortable, searchable table of all successful alternatives ranked by the chosen objective; when no robustness score has been computed, the ranking effectively follows cost
features.specific: Cards for Successful candidates, Controlled regulators and Integrated cost; the best intervention label (for example 'paper k*=0.2, ψ=0.0005' or 'degradation_scale:GATA2×1.5'); a line with target distance, candidates evaluated and Pareto count; and a data table (intervention_id, phenotype, target_distance, cost, controlled_regulator_count) with show/hide columns, search, fullscreen and CSV toolbar. Under Robustness First (screens/027) the rows are effectively sorted by cost, because robustness is null outside the atlas. The toolbar's Download as CSV produced no file in this session.
steps: read the summary cards and the best intervention
scroll the ranked table, including horizontally to hidden columns
compare order under Robustness First vs Sparsity First (both effectively cost-ordered for single compiles)
use the table toolbar (columns, search, fullscreen); its CSV download produced no file
serves_tasks: Compare the ranked alternative interventions by cost and closeness to target
Repeat the design for a second target under a forbidden variable and a cost-first ranking

features.name: 3D state-space trajectory with reference attractors
features.general: Plot a simulated path through a 3-variable state space with the known stable states marked, and let the user rotate, zoom and toggle traces from the legend
features.specific: Plotly 3D 'State-space trajectory' with GATA1/PU.1/GATA2 axes. It draws the G2H→target path and labelled markers for MEP-like, GMP-like, HSC-like and Low-expression CMP-like. The toolbar has zoom, pan, orbital/turntable rotation, camera reset and PNG download.
steps: compile a transition to populate the plot
drag to rotate the view
wheel to zoom
click a legend entry to hide or show an attractor marker
serves_tasks: Inspect the winning intervention's trajectory and time course to confirm it stays at the target after release

features.name: Time series with intervention-release marker
features.general: Plot each variable over time with a vertical line where the intervention stops, so the user can see whether the new state persists after washout
features.specific: 'Regulator dynamics' line chart of GATA1, PU.1 and GATA2 expression against model time, with a dotted 'control released' line. It has a legend toggle, zoom, pan, autoscale and PNG download.
steps: compile a transition
read the curves before and after the 'control released' line
toggle or isolate a regulator via the legend (a double-click hint appears)
zoom into the release window
serves_tasks: Inspect the winning intervention's trajectory and time course to confirm it stays at the target after release

features.name: Reproducible result export (JSON with manifest)
features.general: Download the full result of a run as one file that records inputs, constraints, software versions and content hashes along with the best solution and its trajectory
features.specific: Download compiled transition JSON saves compiled-<start>-<target>-<id>.json. It holds a content_digest; a manifest (classifier, constraints, model_id/version, objective, runtime_versions, search_digest, search_id); the best_candidate (intervention actions with gene, kind, strength, psi, start, duration); and best_trajectory (DOP853 states). The contents come from the saved file. Screens show only the button.
steps: compile a transition
press Download compiled transition JSON
open the file to check the manifest and best candidate
serves_tasks: Export the compiled result for downstream analysis

features.name: Batch all-pairs reachability build with robustness replicate slider
features.general: Run the same search over every ordered pair of reference states under the current constraints, optionally with repeated robustness checks per found edge, to build a reachability graph
features.specific: Reachability atlas tab has a 'Robustness replicates per found edge' slider (0 / 20 / 50 / 200, keyboard-steppable) and a Build reachability atlas button. It compiles all twelve ordered transitions; only persistent successes become graph edges. In this session only the launch controls were seen. A build with GATA1 forbidden, Sparsity First and 0 replicates was started but never finished, so no graph, table or robustness rates were shown.
steps: set constraints and objective in the sidebar
set the robustness replicates slider (0 for speed)
press Build reachability atlas
wait for 'Compiling all twelve ordered transitions…' (did not finish in this session)

features.name: Reference-state verification table
features.general: Tabulate a model's equilibria with coordinates, residual and largest eigenvalue real part to show each is a true, stable fixed point
features.specific: 'Published model reproduction' table with columns phenotype, interpretation, GATA1, PU.1, GATA2, residual ∞-norm, max Re(eigenvalue) and stable. It comes with the regulatory circuit diagram and a citation.
steps: open Reproduction lab
read the residuals and eigenvalues for each attractor
use the table toolbar (columns, CSV, search, fullscreen)
serves_tasks: List the model's stable states with their coordinates, residuals and eigenvalue stability, and confirm that all reference states were verified
